Subject: Follow-up: Reranking model evaluation & next steps

Hi Erin — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery + the initial model-fit takeaways so we’re aligned and can move to a validation A/B plan.

Summary of call:
- Primary objective: Improve search relevance for product results (CTR and downstream purchases).
- Current baseline: in-house BM25 + small BERT re-ranker. You mentioned latency target <= 120ms p95 and budget constraints for hosted inference.

Model-fit recommendations (initial):
- Candidate: redwood-rerank-1 (quantized int8) — best balance of quality and cost in our preload tests.
- Fallback: redwood-rerank-1-small (faster/cheaper) for cold starts and heavy tail.
- Baseline for comparison: your current BERT re-ranker (we used provided eval set).

Benchmarks attached:
- acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_v1.pdf (NDCG@10 / MRR by query slice)
- prompt_set_v3.csv (the prompt/eval set we used; includes query metadata and labels)

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm the evaluation slices to prioritize (head vs long-tail, query intent).
2) Approve the A/B test plan (short 2-week ramp then 4-week analysis) — see ab_test_plan.md attached.
3) Schedule SRE/infra sync for deployment constraints (GPU size, batching, KV cache behavior).

Can you confirm which query slices you care most about and whether the latency target above is firm? We’ll circulate a tighter A/B timeline once we get that.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick questions before we lock the plan: 

1) The NDCG/MRR PDF shows good lift overall, but can you call out which slices drove most of the gain (navigational vs. transactional)? We care most about transactional (purchase intent).
2) What assumptions did you make about the label noise / click labels vs. human relevance? We have noisy click logs that can bias MRR.
3) Latency target is somewhat flexible — p95 <= 150ms is our hard requirement for production, but we'd like p50 closer to 60ms.

If you can call those out, we’ll be comfortable approving the A/B plan. Also please confirm any additional tracking we should add to the hypothesis for product impact.

— Erin
Erin Porter
Product Lead, Search — Acme Corp

Erin — quick answers that should help: 

1) Slice drivers: transactional queries (purchase intent) account for ~65% of the NDCG uplift in the report; navigational boosted head queries but with smaller business impact. See appendix "slice_breakdown" table on page 4 of the PDF.

2) Labels & noise: we ran two label strategies — (A) click-derived pseudo-labels (noisy, larger N) and (B) human-annotated validation set (smaller, higher-quality). Our primary reported numbers use strategy B for final NDCG/MRR to avoid click-bias; we include A in the appendix for scale checks. We flagged high-noise query buckets (low-CTR long-tail) that we excluded from the primary metric.

3) Latency: our int8 quantized pipeline gives p95 ~= 110ms in our dedicated 1xA10 testbed with batching disabled; p50 around ~50–60ms. Fallback small model gives p95 < 60ms but lower NDCG (see trade-off table).

Tracking suggestions for A/B: include CTR@1, CTR@10, add-to-cart rate, conversion rate per query bucket, and business-metric-weighted NDCG. Also track token-level cost and inference errors per model variant.

I attached a short A/B plan and the sliced NDCG table. Happy to jump on a quick call to review.

— Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai)

Attachments: ab_test_plan.md, acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_v1.pdf (sliced appendix)

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reranking model evaluation & next steps

Adding infra notes from the engineering side: 

- Deployment constraints: to meet p95 <= 150ms in Acme's region we recommend dedicated inference nodes (Redwood Dedicated) for the initial A/B ramp — this avoids noisy cold starts. If Acme prefers hosted, we can supply a burst policy but p95 will vary.
- KV cache: for reranking we use per-session KV caching; ensure your request patterns include the query context so we can benefit from prefix caching.
- Rollout plan suggestion:
  * Phase 0 (canary): 5% traffic for 3 days — validate latency, basic metrics.
  * Phase 1 (ramp): 30% traffic for 2 weeks — collect business metrics and slice-level NDCG/MRR.
  * Phase 2 (full): remaining traffic with monitoring and auto-fallback to baseline on error rates.

I recommend instrumenting a small latency budget (e.g., drop to fallback if tail > 180ms) and expose model-version tags in logs for post-hoc analysis.

— Vivek
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
